solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plants in island thus smuggled from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means the run of letters is read right to left

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, as printed in quotations
to run guns or drugs is to smuggle them, so smuggled gives ran

explanation.surface: Specimen plants have been sneaked out of an island and brought in from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns ISSICRAN round to give the answer; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Daffodils and jonquils are the spring flowers of the genus Narcissus, so the plural names a group of plants.

clue.text: Sea nymph entangled in reed

indicators.note: things entangled are knotted up and jumbled, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A water spirit has got herself caught up among the rushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entangled' rearranges the six letters of IN REED.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the fifty daughters of Nereus were sea nymphs, each one a member of this group.

clue.text: Dairy product a girl takes in bed

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it within, so the girl's name wraps round the bed

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name, one of many a setter can call a girl
a cot is a small bed, typically a child's

explanation.surface: A young woman eats a cheese snack while lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a girl' is a stock crossword source of any girl's name; 'takes in' makes her name the outer piece, wrapped round the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft Italian whey cheese is something made from milk, so it is a dairy product.

clue.text: Put friend in the picture in a relaxed way

parts.note: to put someone in the picture is to tell them the facts, so with 'Put' the phrase means inform
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Bringing a pal up to date casually, without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put ... in the picture' is one idiom with 'friend' as its object, so the clue reads as inform ally; 'Put' belongs to the idiom rather than giving letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Done casually or without ceremony is done without formality, the adverb for a relaxed manner.

clue.text: Serving in army club, one left out cementing tool

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so the letter for one is dropped from the army word

parts.note: serving in the army is soldiering
I is the Roman numeral for one
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A soldier and his golf club, with a tool that does the cementing, all in one line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes the I from SOLDIERING to leave SOLDERING.
explanation.definitionFit: Solder joins metal parts, so the heated tool used to apply it cements pieces together.

clue.text: Like a Dane, for example — and not one in Washington

parts.note: nor means and not, as in neither this nor that

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so the letter for one goes inside the city

parts.note: Washington DC is the US capital, abbreviated DC
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Dane is Scandinavian, and none of them lives in the American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington' is the city, shortened to its District of Columbia letters; 'in' places the Roman one inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Danes, Swedes and Norwegians are all Scandinavians, the peoples of northern Europe called by this adjective.

clue.text: Tender-sounding Mercian king?

indicators.note: something sounding like a word is heard as it, so the clue's verb is said aloud

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as in tendering a bid

explanation.surface: A query about a gentle-sounding ruler of an old English kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, OFFER in a non-rhotic British accent comes out the same as the king's name.
explanation.definitionFit: He ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia in the eighth century and built the dyke named after him.

clue.text: Republican in seedy bar visiting cinema, perhaps

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so the party letter goes inside the bar

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar or club
someone visiting is in, at the place

explanation.surface: A Republican politician slumming in a sleazy bar before taking in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does the insertion, while 'visiting' only supplies letters of its own; 'perhaps' marks the cinema as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor movie theatre watched from parked cars is one kind of cinema, which is why 'perhaps' is there.

clue.text: Scorn fiddle casual worker finally bought

parts.note: a fiddle is a swindle, a con
a temp is a temporary worker

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word that follows, so only its closing letter is used

explanation.surface: Disdain for the cheating temp who was eventually bought off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives T, the last letter of 'bought'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn and this word are synonyms, both meaning a feeling that someone is worthless or beneath notice.

clue.text: Legendary bird biting head off dangerous reptile

indicators.note: biting the head off something removes its first part, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: croc is short for crocodile, a dangerous reptile

explanation.surface: A mythical bird decapitates a crocodile with its beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting head off' drops the first C of CROC.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arabian tales such as Sinbad's voyages this giant bird of prey carries off elephants, so it is mythical.

clue.text: Fine workforce, one possessed by man like Sir John?

parts.note: F stands for fine, as on pencil grades

indicators.note: something possessed by another is held within it, so the staff and one sit inside the man's name

parts.note: Alan is a man's name
staff are a workforce
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fine workforce, with one member owned by a knightly figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possessed by' makes the man's name the container; 'Sir John' points to Shakespeare's knight rather than any real person.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat, jovial, boastful knight, so the adjective describes anyone resembling him.

clue.text: Insensitively considered the French devious

parts.note: considered means thought, as in thought about
les is the French plural for the
devious means sly or cunning

explanation.surface: The French, considered devious, are judged in a rather unkind way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' gives LES, a French word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without considering others' feelings is acting carelessly or tactlessly, the same idea as insensitive conduct.

clue.text: Briefly poke around leg, to find protein

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the final letter of the verb goes

parts.note: to poke around in others' affairs is to meddle or interfere
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so leg gives ON

explanation.surface: A doctor prods quickly around a leg in search of a protein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims INTERFERE to INTERFER. ON = leg is a cricket term: the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Interferons are signalling proteins the body releases in response to viruses, so the word names one kind of protein.

clue.text: Share the Sunday joint, do we hear?

indicators.note: asking what we hear points to a spoken version, so the joint's word is said aloud

parts.note: a Sunday joint is a roast of meat

explanation.surface: A question about carving up the Sunday roast between the family.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sunday joint is the traditional British roast of meat eaten at Sunday lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to distribute or allot portions, so the verb means to share.

clue.text: Recipients of letter from Welshwoman cutting business deficit

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: a thing cutting another slices into its middle, so the woman's name goes inside the deficit

parts.note: a deficit is a loss
Sian is a Welsh woman's name

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman trims a business's shortfall, and someone receives a letter about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' sends the Welsh name into the deficit word; 'letter' is not a written character but one of St Paul's epistles.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul's Epistle to the Colossians was written to the church at Colossae, so its readers were the addressees of an epistle.

clue.text: Ragout of game containing a highly seasoned sausage

indicators.note: one thing containing another holds it inside, so the letter goes within the stew

parts.note: a salmi is a ragout of game birds, partly roasted then stewed

explanation.surface: A game stew with a spicy sausage thrown into the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ragout' wants to be an anagram signal, but the whole phrase is the dish SALMI; 'containing' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian cured pork sausage is flavoured with garlic and spices, so it is strongly seasoned.

clue.text: Mature combination of companies adopting western name

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the two letters are taken inside the companies' word

parts.note: a group is a set of companies under common ownership

explanation.surface: A seasoned conglomerate takes on a western name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' puts WN inside GROUP: GRO-WN-UP.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult has reached full development, so the adjective means mature, fully grown in mind and body.

clue.text: Insect — one flapping lamely at first in farm pen

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so these letters go within the pen

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs on a farm

indicators.note: at first points to the start of each of the two words before it, so their opening letters are used

explanation.surface: An insect, beating its wings feebly, ends up trapped in a pigsty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' works on both 'flapping' and 'lamely'; 'in' then places all of that inside the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: This winged insect of the order Plecoptera breeds in streams and is a favourite model for anglers' flies.

clue.text: Delay after chap encounters strong wind from east

parts.note: Tim is a man's name, a chap

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from east means the word is read right to left

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A man held up when he runs into a strong easterly wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from east' reverses only the wind, since 'encounters' and 'after' are just links joining it to the chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A lag is a gap in time between cause and effect, so this compound means a period of delay.

clue.text: Effeminate chap writing about class work

indicators.note: one thing about another goes round it, so the manuscript letters surround the class word

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
ilk means kind or class, as in people of that ilk
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A weak young man composes an essay on class for an assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the manuscript abbreviation the container; 'work' is the standard op, short for opus.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak, timid man lacking courage is a milquetoast or softy, dated slang for an unmanly fellow.

clue.text: Switching sides, Chinese communist finds Lao Zi's philosophy

indicators.note: the two end letters, the sides of the word, swap places

parts.note: a follower of Mao Zedong is a Maoist, a Chinese communist

explanation.surface: A defecting Chinese communist turns to an ancient philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switching sides' swaps the first and last letters of MAOIST, M and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Lao Zi, author of the Tao Te Ching, founded this Chinese tradition centred on the Way, or Tao.

clue.text: Language provoked by a limited rise in Westminster?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the postcode

parts.note: SW1 is the London postcode for Westminster, with the 1 read as I

indicators.note: something limited is cut short, so the final letter of the rise is lost

parts.note: a hill is a rise in the ground

explanation.surface: A small pay rise provokes some choice language in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster's London postcode is SW1, the digit read as the letter I. 'limited' trims the rise and 'in' puts it, after A, inside the postcode; 'provoked by' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: This Bantu tongue is widely spoken across East Africa, a lingua franca of Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Stick a poster, possibly, in this place

parts.note: a poster is one example of an advertisement, an ad
in this place means here

explanation.surface: An instruction to glue up a poster on this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals that a poster is one kind of AD.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling or be fixed to a surface is to stick to it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Retired priest following northern river

indicators.note: the priest's letters come after, following the northern letter
something retired has gone back, so the priest's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A clergyman retires to the north and settles by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the Old Testament priest, a crossword favourite. 'Retired' reverses him and 'following' places him after the northern letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the great African river flowing north through Egypt to the Mediterranean, the world's longest.

clue.text: Grassy area in politician's part of constituency

parts.note: a Green is a member of the Green Party, so politician's gives GREEN plus the possessive S
a ward is an electoral division within a constituency

explanation.surface: A patch of lawn in an MP's local district.
explanation.walkthrough: A ward is a local electoral division, smaller than a parliamentary constituency in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Sward is turf, so this compound means a stretch of grass-covered ground.

clue.text: Long evergreen tree

definitions.meaning: to long for something is to yearn or ache for it
a coniferous tree with needles, such as the Scots variety

explanation.surface: A tall tree that keeps its leaves all year.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to yearn; as a noun it is the familiar needled conifer.

clue.text: Worried if a host is an obsessive trendy!

indicators.note: worried can mean shaken or tugged about, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nervous hostess frets that a guest is fixated on what is in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' rearranges the eleven letters of IF A HOST IS AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to following the latest styles is a fashion follower, a trendy with a fixation on clothes.

clue.text: Anger shown when state's leader is deposed

indicators.note: a deposed leader is removed from the front, so the first letter goes; the letters of 'leader is' read backwards happen to contain the answer, a coincidence the setter did not intend

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name of the state of Ireland

explanation.surface: Popular fury erupts when a country's ruler is overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader is deposed' drops the first E of EIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary synonym for wrath or rage, the same feeling as anger.

clue.text: Current Oxford course taken in six months? That's wonderful!

indicators.note: something taken in is held inside, so these letters go within the half-year

parts.note: six months is half a year, so the first half of the word year
I is the symbol for electric current
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, a degree course at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student cheers after finishing a half-year Oxford course.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE (Philosophy, Politics and Economics) is a famous Oxford degree; 'six months' is half of a year, so half the word. 'taken in' sets current and course inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cry of joy or delight, the sort of exclamation that greets wonderful news.

clue.text: Lower rent Ray's splashed out up front?

indicators.note: up front means placed ahead, so the jumbled letters come before the rent word
splashed out suggests letters scattered about, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: to hire something is to rent it

explanation.surface: Ray spent lavishly on a deposit to cut the rent he pays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not 'reduce' but something that lows, a cow; Ayrshires are a Scottish dairy breed. 'splashed out' rearranges RAYS into AYRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle low, so a lower is a cow, and this Scottish dairy breed is one such animal.
